Topic 2.3: Linear Inequalities
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Inequalities, part of Algebra 2.2 Linear Equations (6 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learn in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use linear inequalities in real life? 2. Why do we use linear inequalities in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Use inequality cards in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals to complete simple inequality statements using symbols. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any alternative functional part of the body or assistive devices to carry out the activity.

2. Use inequality cards/objects to form simple linear inequalities with one unknown.

3. Draw/ trace/stamp/mount in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals and represent simple inequality statements on a number line. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative part of the body or assistive technology to draw and represent simple inequality.

4. Use inequality cards to 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Use inequality cards in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals to complete simple inequality statements using symbols. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any alternative functional part of the body or assistive devices to carry out the activity.
2. Use inequality cards/objects to form simple linear inequalities with one unknown.
3. Draw/ trace/stamp/mount in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals and represent simple inequality statements on a number line. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative part of the body or assistive technology to draw and represent simple inequality.
4. Use inequality cards to 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Inequalities together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

● Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses on how to form the linear inequalities.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner draws and represents inequality statements on a number line.

Values

Integrity: as the learner observes and adheres to the conditions of the given inequalities.
